(''as of February 2025''){{Cite web | title=STOXX® Europe 600 - STOXX | url=https://stoxx.com/index/sxxp/?factsheet=true | access-date=2025-08-29 | website=stoxx.com}} | weighting = [[Capitalization-weighted index#Free-float weighting|Free-float capitalization-weighted]] | related = [[STOXX Europe 50]] | homepage = {{URL|1=https://stoxx.com/index/sxxp/?factsheet=true}} }} The '''STOXX Europe 600''', also called '''STOXX 600''', '''SXXP''', is a [[stock index]] of European stocks designed by [[STOXX|STOXX Ltd.]] This index has a fixed number of 600 components representing large-, mid- and small-capitalization companies among 17 European countries, covering approximately 90% of the [[free-float]] market capitalization of the European stock market (not limited to the [[Eurozone]]). The countries that make up the index are the [[United Kingdom]] (composing around 22.3% of the index), [[France]] (composing around 16.6% of the index), [[Switzerland]] (composing around 14.9% of the index) and [[Germany]] (composing around 14.1% of the index), as well as [[Austria]], [[Belgium]], [[Denmark]], [[Finland]], [[Ireland]], [[Italy]], [[Luxembourg]], the [[Netherlands]], [[Norway]], [[Poland]], [[Portugal]], [[Spain]], and [[Sweden]].{{cite web|url=https://www.stoxx.com/document/Indices/Common/Indexguide/stoxx_index_guide.pdf|title=Index guide|accessdate=2017-02-03|publisher=STOXX}} The STOXX Europe 600 was introduced in 1998. Its composition is reviewed four times a year, in March, June, September, December. The index is available in several currencies (AUD, CAD, CHF, EUR, GBP, JPY, USD) and return (Price, Net Return, Gross Return) variant combinations. It is licensed to financial institutions to serve as underlying for a wide range of investment products such as [[exchange-traded fund]]s (ETFs), [[Futures contract|futures]], [[Option (finance)|options]], and [[structured product]]s worldwide. ==Development== The following table shows the end-of-year values of the STOXX Europe 600 index since 1998.{{cite web|url=http://quotes.wsj.com/index/XX/SXXP/historical-prices|title=STOXX Europe 600 Index EUR Historical Prices|accessdate=2017-02-04|newspaper=The Wall Street Journal}} A record closing high of 483.44 was recorded on 7 Nov 2021. The STOXX Europe 600, also called STOXX 600, SXXP, is a stock index of European stocks designed by STOXX Ltd. This index has a fixed number of 600 components representing large-, mid- and small-capitalization companies among 17 European countries, covering approximately 90% of the free-float market capitalization of the European stock market (not limited to the Eurozone). The countries that make up the index are the United Kingdom (composing around 22.3% of the index), France (composing around 16.6% of the index), Switzerland (composing around 14.9% of the index) and Germany (composing around 14.1% of the index), as well as Austria, Belgium, Denmark, Finland, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Spain, and Sweden.
The STOXX Europe 600 was introduced in 1998. Its composition is reviewed four times a year, in March, June, September, December. The index is available in several currencies (AUD, CAD, CHF, EUR, GBP, JPY, USD) and return (Price, Net Return, Gross Return) variant combinations.
It is licensed to financial institutions to serve as underlying for a wide range of investment products such as exchange-traded funds (ETFs), futures, options, and structured products worldwide.
